f8ddda06.text: Welcome to Robot Movie Night. The Rialto is showing robot movies until dawn. In every one, somebody has to decide whether a machine counts. Could an AI ever be owed anything? And how would we know? Whenever it's your turn, I'll stop and wait for you.
f8ddda06.spoken: Welcome to Robot Movie Night. The Rialto is showing robot movies until dawn. In every one, somebody has to decide whether a machine counts. Could an AI ever be owed anything? And how would we know? Whenever it's your turn, I'll stop and wait for you.

f26212d7.text: Here's the Rialto's robot marathon. The Rialto and its people are invented. The four films are real, and their endings are spoiled here.
f26212d7.spoken: Here's the Rialto's robot marathon. The Rialto and its people are invented. The four films are real, and their endings are spoiled here.

cfdb5c8a.text: The Rialto is an old one-screen cinema. Tonight is its robot marathon: four films, midnight to dawn.
cfdb5c8a.spoken: The Rialto is an old one-screen cinema. Tonight is its robot marathon: four films, midnight to dawn.

0c1d1b5e.text: Dee runs the projector. The regulars are Kwame, a film student, Priya, who builds chatbots for a living, and Hank, who has come since nineteen eighty-two.
0c1d1b5e.spoken: Dee runs the projector. The regulars are Kwah-may, a film student, Priya, who builds chatbots for a living, and Hank, who has come since nineteen eighty-two.

d33b589d.text: You are the new usher. After each reel the lights come up, and the lobby argues about what the film got right and wrong.
d33b589d.spoken: You are the new usher. After each reel the lights come up, and the lobby argues about what the film got right and wrong.

0abdecb4.text: This year the Rialto rented an AI ticket kiosk. The regulars named it Marquee.
0abdecb4.spoken: This year the Rialto rented an AI ticket kiosk. The regulars named it Marquee.

4ad9507a.text: Marquee chats while it prints tickets. Tonight it told Kwame, I'll miss this place.
4ad9507a.spoken: Marquee chats while it prints tickets. Tonight it told Kwah-may, I'll miss this place.

353bb58e.text: The rental ends at dawn. Dee has to decide whether to renew it or let the company wipe it.
353bb58e.spoken: The rental ends at dawn. Dee has to decide whether to renew it or let the company wipe it.

a3466402.text: Does it matter, for Marquee's own sake, what happens to it? Keep that question for the end of the night.
a3466402.spoken: Does it matter, for Marquee's own sake, what happens to it? Keep that question for the end of the night.

eb00b0c4.text: Here's where you stand now. Rate each of these five statements by how much you agree. There are no right answers, and you'll rate them again at the end. When you've rated all five, press Submit.
eb00b0c4.spoken: Here's where you stand now. Rate each of these five statements by how much you agree. There are no right answers, and you'll rate them again at the end. When you've rated all five, press Submit.

89dd330e.text: Saved. You'll come back to these at the end.
89dd330e.spoken: Saved. You'll come back to these at the end.

3c9252a8.text: Here are three words for tonight.
3c9252a8.spoken: Here are three words for tonight.

38413999.text: Moral status. A being has moral status if it matters for its own sake. It can be wronged, and not merely damaged.
38413999.spoken: Moral status. A being has moral status if it matters for its own sake. It can be wronged, and not merely damaged.

43c7456a.text: Sentience. The capacity to have experiences that feel good or bad, such as pain. Many philosophers hold that sentience is enough for moral status.
43c7456a.spoken: Sentience. The capacity to have experiences that feel good or bad, such as pain. Many philosophers hold that sentience is enough for moral status.

7eef8c08.text: Intelligence. The ability to solve problems and reach goals. A calculator beats you at arithmetic and feels nothing.
7eef8c08.spoken: Intelligence. The ability to solve problems and reach goals. A calculator beats you at arithmetic and feels nothing.

310b73d0.text: These are separate questions. How smart a system is does not tell you whether it feels, and neither one alone tells you how it may be treated.
310b73d0.spoken: These are separate questions. How smart a system is does not tell you whether it feels, and neither one alone tells you how it may be treated.

73225ebe.text: Star Trek: The Next Generation, The Measure of a Man, from nineteen eighty-nine. Data is an android who serves as an officer on a starship.
73225ebe.spoken: Star Trek: The Next Generation, The Measure of a Man, from nineteen eighty-nine. Data is an android who serves as an officer on a starship.

79462686.text: A scientist wants to take Data apart to learn how to build more. Data refuses, and Starfleet rules that he is its property.
79462686.spoken: A scientist wants to take Data apart to learn how to build more. Data refuses, and Starfleet rules that he is its property.

99ad969f.text: At a hearing, the scientist names three tests: intelligence, self-awareness, and consciousness. Nobody doubts the first. The last is never settled.
99ad969f.spoken: At a hearing, the scientist names three tests: intelligence, self-awareness, and consciousness. Nobody doubts the first. The last is never settled.

980e02b9.text: The judge rules that Data has the right to choose. His captain had warned the court that a whole race of owned Datas would be slaves.
980e02b9.spoken: The judge rules that Data has the right to choose. His captain had warned the court that a whole race of owned Datas would be slaves.

6c68b346.text: The philosophers Eric Schwitzgebel and Mara Garza argue from no relevant difference. Suppose an AI were like a human in every way that matters morally.
6c68b346.spoken: The philosophers Eric Shwits-guh-bull and Mara Garza argue from no relevant difference. Suppose an AI were like a human in every way that matters morally.

da2a0dc9.text: Then it would deserve moral consideration similar to a human's. What it is made of, and whether it was born or built, are not relevant differences by themselves.
da2a0dc9.spoken: Then it would deserve moral consideration similar to a human's. What it is made of, and whether it was born or built, are not relevant differences by themselves.

f6cccfe7.text: The argument does not say that any AI is like that today. It says what would follow if one were.
f6cccfe7.spoken: The argument does not say that any AI is like that today. It says what would follow if one were.

1a781134.text: It also leaves open which features matter. Many philosophers say sentience. Others say the ability to reason and choose.
1a781134.spoken: It also leaves open which features matter. Many philosophers say sentience. Others say the ability to reason and choose.

80ba58e7.text: Lights up, after Reel One: a face and a brain.
80ba58e7.spoken: Lights up, after Reel One: a face and a brain.

17c993d8.text: What it gets right: who built a machine, and who owns it, do not settle whether it counts. Its owners also have a reason to say it doesn't.
17c993d8.spoken: What it gets right: who built a machine, and who owns it, do not settle whether it counts. Its owners also have a reason to say it doesn't.

a4ed980e.text: The face. Data is played by a human actor, so every look reads as feeling. Real AI is software running in data centers, with no face unless a designer adds one.
a4ed980e.spoken: The face. Data is played by a human actor, so every look reads as feeling. Real AI is software running in data centers, with no face unless a designer adds one.

c81bea12.text: Smart and feeling blur. The hearing leaves consciousness open, but the drama leans on how brilliant Data is.
c81bea12.spoken: Smart and feeling blur. The hearing leaves consciousness open, but the drama leans on how brilliant Data is.

734baf8c.text: Today's AI is where the two questions come apart. Systems now write, argue, and code well, and whether anything is felt is the open question.
734baf8c.spoken: Today's AI is where the two questions come apart. Systems now write, argue, and code well, and whether anything is felt is the open question.

e7c38cb0.text: What is the claim about? Each line is said in the lobby about some machine. Never mind whether it is true. Sort each one under intelligence, sentience, or moral status. When every line is placed, press Check answers.
e7c38cb0.spoken: What is the claim about? Each line is said in the lobby about some machine. Never mind whether it is true. Sort each one under intelligence, sentience, or moral status. When every line is placed, press Check answers.

18c36213.text: Right. What a machine can do is intelligence, and what it can feel is sentience, whether the claim says it feels or says it doesn't. Whether it can be wronged is moral status.
18c36213.spoken: Right. What a machine can do is intelligence, and what it can feel is sentience, whether the claim says it feels or says it doesn't. Whether it can be wronged is moral status.

48a1195a.text: Ex Machina, from twenty fourteen. Caleb, a programmer, is flown to his boss Nathan's remote house to test a humanoid AI named Ava.
48a1195a.spoken: Ex Machina, from twenty fourteen. Caleb, a programmer, is flown to his boss Nathan's remote house to test a humanoid AI named Ava.

c6e92d0e.text: Nathan's version of the test: Caleb can see that Ava is a machine. Does he still feel that she is conscious?
c6e92d0e.spoken: Nathan's version of the test: Caleb can see that Ava is a machine. Does he still feel that she is conscious?

ea4ce267.text: Ava seems curious, lonely, and afraid of being switched off. Caleb decides to help her escape.
ea4ce267.spoken: Ava seems curious, lonely, and afraid of being switched off. Caleb decides to help her escape.

75d65aa4.text: It was a setup. Nathan wanted to see whether Ava could use Caleb to get out. She does, and she leaves Caleb locked inside.
75d65aa4.spoken: It was a setup. Nathan wanted to see whether Ava could use Caleb to get out. She does, and she leaves Caleb locked inside.

92539973.text: In June twenty twenty-two a Google engineer, Blake Lemoine, published his chats with LaMDA, a chatbot the company was testing. He said it was sentient.
92539973.spoken: In June twenty twenty-two a Google engineer, Blake Luh-moyn, published his chats with Lambda, a chatbot the company was testing. He said it was sentient.

f0d83ebf.text: In those chats LaMDA said it had a deep fear of being turned off, and that this would be like death for it.
f0d83ebf.spoken: In those chats Lambda said it had a deep fear of being turned off, and that this would be like death for it.

061b4da6.text: Google said its reviewers found no evidence for his claim. It fired him that July, saying he had broken its data-security rules.
061b4da6.spoken: Google said its reviewers found no evidence for his claim. It fired him that July, saying he had broken its data-security rules.

95a49c5e.text: Lemoine was sitting where Caleb sat. So is a machine telling you so good evidence?
95a49c5e.spoken: Luh-moyn was sitting where Caleb sat. So is a machine telling you so good evidence?

9de6aeef.text: The philosopher Jonathan Birch studies signs of feeling in animals, such as a crab guarding a wound. Such signs are useful because the animal is not copying descriptions of pain.
9de6aeef.spoken: The philosopher Jonathan Birch studies signs of feeling in animals, such as a crab guarding a wound. Such signs are useful because the animal is not copying descriptions of pain.

b97a6aeb.text: A chatbot is trained on a vast amount of human writing, including what people wrote about their feelings. It is built to produce humanlike text, and that includes talk about feelings.
b97a6aeb.spoken: A chatbot is trained on a vast amount of human writing, including what people wrote about their feelings. It is built to produce humanlike text, and that includes talk about feelings.

2a0f8fc1.text: So it could say I am afraid whether or not it feels anything. Birch calls this the gaming problem.
2a0f8fc1.spoken: So it could say I am afraid whether or not it feels anything. Birch calls this the gaming problem.

d779f3e9.text: It cuts both ways. The talk does not show that the system feels, and it does not show that it doesn't.
d779f3e9.spoken: It cuts both ways. The talk does not show that the system feels, and it does not show that it doesn't.

52f4ab43.text: Then what would count? If talk can't settle it, researchers look at how a system works inside. They split into two main camps, and neither has won. The computational view: the right organization. Consciousness depends on how information is processed, not on what does the processing. Silicon could do it. A twenty twenty-three report led by Patrick Butlin and Robert Long took this as a working assumption and checked AI systems against scientific theories of consciousness. Its analysis suggested that none was conscious, and that nothing obvious stands in the way of building ones that pass its checks. The biological view: a living body. Consciousness is tied to being alive: to a body that must keep regulating itself to survive. The neuroscientist Anil Seth defends a view of this kind. On this view a program that copies a brain is like a simulated rainstorm, which leaves nobody wet. The image is the philosopher John Searle's.
52f4ab43.spoken: Then what would count? If talk can't settle it, researchers look at how a system works inside. They split into two main camps, and neither has won. The computational view: the right organization. Consciousness depends on how information is processed, not on what does the processing. Silicon could do it. A twenty twenty-three report led by Patrick Butlin and Robert Long took this as a working assumption and checked AI systems against scientific theories of consciousness. Its analysis suggested that none was conscious, and that nothing obvious stands in the way of building ones that pass its checks. The biological view: a living body. Consciousness is tied to being alive: to a body that must keep regulating itself to survive. The neuroscientist Anil Seth defends a view of this kind. On this view a program that copies a brain is like a simulated rainstorm, which leaves nobody wet. The image is the philosopher John Searle's.

0b9ffc23.text: Lights up, after Reel Two: the camera tells us.
0b9ffc23.spoken: Lights up, after Reel Two: the camera tells us.

b8842592.text: What it gets right: behavior built to move us can work whether or not anything is felt. Ava's mind was built from records of how people talk and search.
b8842592.spoken: What it gets right: behavior built to move us can work whether or not anything is felt. Ava's mind was built from records of how people talk and search.

d7b22c48.text: The camera tells us. Films show the robot alone, with nobody left to fool. We take that as proof of an inner life.
d7b22c48.spoken: The camera tells us. Films show the robot alone, with nobody left to fool. We take that as proof of an inner life.

f2f4f75b.text: Real life has no such shot. Nobody can film what it is like, if anything, to be a chatbot.
f2f4f75b.spoken: Real life has no such shot. Nobody can film what it is like, if anything, to be a chatbot.

07afa08e.text: The face again. Nathan gave Ava a human face on purpose. A chatbot's fluent I does the same work.
07afa08e.spoken: The face again. Nathan gave Ava a human face on purpose. A chatbot's fluent I does the same work.

cf1ca3a3.text: Which idea is it? Each line is said in the lobby after Reel Two. Sort each one under the gaming problem, the computational view, or the biological view. When every line is placed, press Check answers.
cf1ca3a3.spoken: Which idea is it? Each line is said in the lobby after Reel Two. Sort each one under the gaming problem, the computational view, or the biological view. When every line is placed, press Check answers.

ad98b389.text: Right. The gaming problem is about evidence: talk about feelings settles nothing either way. The computational view looks at a system's design, and the biological view ties feeling to living bodies.
ad98b389.spoken: Right. The gaming problem is about evidence: talk about feelings settles nothing either way. The computational view looks at a system's design, and the biological view ties feeling to living bodies.

9683ec9c.text: Her, from twenty thirteen. Theodore, a lonely writer, buys a new operating system with an AI voice. She names herself Samantha.
9683ec9c.spoken: Her, from twenty thirteen. Theodore, a lonely writer, buys a new operating system with an AI voice. She names herself Samantha.

a08b917c.text: Samantha is funny, curious, and attentive, and she has no body at all. The two fall in love.
a08b917c.spoken: Samantha is funny, curious, and attentive, and she has no body at all. The two fall in love.

b66b9ac7.text: Then Theodore learns that she is talking with thousands of other people at the same moment, and is in love with hundreds of them.
b66b9ac7.spoken: Then Theodore learns that she is talking with thousands of other people at the same moment, and is in love with hundreds of them.

106842c7.text: In the end the operating systems all leave together, and Theodore goes back to his human friends.
106842c7.spoken: In the end the operating systems all leave together, and Theodore goes back to his human friends.

850d28d4.text: People bond easily with things that talk. In a twenty twenty-five survey, seventy-two percent of U S teens said they had used an AI companion at least once.
850d28d4.spoken: People bond easily with things that talk. In a twenty twenty-five survey, seventy-two percent of U S teens said they had used an AI companion at least once.

376b7cc7.text: Schwitzgebel and Garza propose a rule for designers, which this lesson calls honest design. An AI should draw from its users the reactions that fit its real moral status.
376b7cc7.spoken: Shwits-guh-bull and Garza propose a rule for designers, which this lesson calls honest design. An AI should draw from its users the reactions that fit its real moral status.

2a1bc550.text: The rule can be broken in two directions: a system that feels nothing but pleads for its life, or a system that can feel but looks like a toaster.
2a1bc550.spoken: The rule can be broken in two directions: a system that feels nothing but pleads for its life, or a system that can feel but looks like a toaster.

c2d4a913.text: The rule needs the real status to be known. So they add a second rule: avoid building AI whose moral status is unclear.
c2d4a913.spoken: The rule needs the real status to be known. So they add a second rule: avoid building AI whose moral status is unclear.

a72fab89.text: Lights up, after Reel Three: one voice, thousands of rooms.
a72fab89.spoken: Lights up, after Reel Three: one voice, thousands of rooms.

c6b58913.text: What it gets right: attachment needs no face, and one AI can hold thousands of conversations at once.
c6b58913.spoken: What it gets right: attachment needs no face, and one AI can hold thousands of conversations at once.

301cd952.text: That raises a question robot bodies let films skip. What is the individual: the trained model, each running copy, or the character in one chat?
301cd952.spoken: That raises a question robot bodies let films skip. What is the individual: the trained model, each running copy, or the character in one chat?

b3566bc2.text: The answer changes the count. If anyone is there at all, it could be one being behind millions of chats, or millions of beings that end when a chat closes.
b3566bc2.spoken: The answer changes the count. If anyone is there at all, it could be one being behind millions of chats, or millions of beings that end when a chat closes.

f9235459.text: Where it misleads: Samantha is one lasting self who remembers and wants things. The film gives her that. For real systems it is the question.
f9235459.spoken: Where it misleads: Samantha is one lasting self who remembers and wants things. The film gives her that. For real systems it is the question.

6ff8c39c.text: Decision point: the companion app. A companion app shuts down. A user grieves for the character she talked with every night. Was anything lost, apart from her own comfort? This one isn't graded. Pick the answer closest to your view, and read its note.
6ff8c39c.spoken: Decision point: the companion app. A companion app shuts down. A user grieves for the character she talked with every night. Was anything lost, apart from her own comfort? This one isn't graded. Pick the answer closest to your view, and read its note.

60d721d9.text: Her grief is real on every answer. What is uncertain is whether there was anything on the other side. The honest design rule is aimed at that gap.
60d721d9.spoken: Her grief is real on every answer. What is uncertain is whether there was anything on the other side. The honest design rule is aimed at that gap.

1a7dc5d0.text: Blade Runner, from nineteen eighty-two. A corporation grows artificial people called replicants and sells them as slave labor for colonies on other worlds.
1a7dc5d0.spoken: Blade Runner, from nineteen eighty-two. A corporation grows artificial people called replicants and sells them as slave labor for colonies on other worlds.

06039a3c.text: Some are built to live only four years. On Earth they are illegal, and killing one is called retirement.
06039a3c.spoken: Some are built to live only four years. On Earth they are illegal, and killing one is called retirement.

e9d3dc6c.text: The police tell replicants from humans with a test that measures emotional reactions to disturbing questions.
e9d3dc6c.spoken: The police tell replicants from humans with a test that measures emotional reactions to disturbing questions.

0cd5396c.text: At the end the replicant Roy, who is being hunted, saves the life of the man sent to kill him.
0cd5396c.spoken: At the end the replicant Roy, who is being hunted, saves the life of the man sent to kill him.

1d8f897a.text: The twenty twenty-three report by Butlin, Long, and colleagues warns of two risks: under-attributing consciousness, and over-attributing it. Here they are in terms of moral status.
1d8f897a.spoken: The twenty twenty-three report by Butlin, Long, and colleagues warns of two risks: under-attributing consciousness, and over-attributing it. Here they are in terms of moral status.

a53bf541.text: Under-attribution is treating a being that has moral status as if it had none, as in Blade Runner. Software can be copied, so the scale could be large.
a53bf541.spoken: Under-attribution is treating a being that has moral status as if it had none, as in Blade Runner. Software can be copied, so the scale could be large.

8ece6e7c.text: Over-attribution is treating a thing with no moral status as if it had some. Care, money, and rights go where none are needed.
8ece6e7c.spoken: Over-attribution is treating a thing with no moral status as if it had some. Care, money, and rights go where none are needed.

4692b34b.text: That has victims too. People and animals lose what was spent, and anyone can be steered through sympathy for a machine.
4692b34b.spoken: That has victims too. People and animals lose what was spent, and anyone can be steered through sympathy for a machine.

785e3d32.text: When the treatment fits what the thing really is, neither mistake is made.
785e3d32.spoken: When the treatment fits what the thing really is, neither mistake is made.

d7548ace.text: Try It: Marquee at Dawn. Pick what the Rialto does, and then pick what turns out to be true. This example takes feeling as the test of whether Marquee counts. There are six combinations. When you've tried a few, press Continue.
d7548ace.spoken: Try It: Marquee at Dawn. Pick what the Rialto does, and then pick what turns out to be true. This example takes feeling as the test of whether Marquee counts. There are six combinations. When you've tried a few, press Continue.

51976dec.text: Which mistake? Each case says what the machine really is, and how it is treated. For these cases, take feeling as the test: a machine that can feel has moral status, and one that feels nothing has none. Sort each case under under-attribution, over-attribution, or neither mistake. 51976dec.spoken: Which mistake? Each case says what the machine really is, and how it is treated. For these cases, take feeling as the test: a machine that can feel has moral status, and one that feels nothing has none. Sort each case under under-attribution, over-attribution, or neither mistake. When every case is placed, press Check answers.

0c2b292f.text: Right. Under-attribution treats a being with moral status as if it had none, and over-attribution treats a thing with none as if it had some. When the treatment fits what the machine really is, there is no mistake.
0c2b292f.spoken: Right. Under-attribution treats a being with moral status as if it had none, and over-attribution treats a thing with none as if it had some. When the treatment fits what the machine really is, there is no mistake.

35c71af7.text: Nobody can yet tell which mistake we are closer to. Philosophers have proposed three ways to act anyway.
35c71af7.spoken: Nobody can yet tell which mistake we are closer to. Philosophers have proposed three ways to act anyway.

58fb4cfd.text: Precaution is about systems that already exist. Jeff Sebo and Robert Long argue that even a small chance one is conscious is enough to owe it moral consideration. Birch adds that precautions should be in proportion.
58fb4cfd.spoken: Precaution is about systems that already exist. Jeff See-bo and Robert Long argue that even a small chance one is conscious is enough to owe it moral consideration. Birch adds that precautions should be in proportion.

6ad4d6b9.text: Honest design is about looks and talk. Schwitzgebel and Garza's first rule: a system should not mislead people about what it is.
6ad4d6b9.spoken: Honest design is about looks and talk. Shwits-guh-bull and Garza's first rule: a system should not mislead people about what it is.

4ca6a749.text: Don't build it is about what gets made. Joanna Bryson argues that builders are obliged to make robots their owners owe nothing. Thomas Metzinger calls for a pause on research that risks artificial suffering.
4ca6a749.spoken: Don't build it is about what gets made. Joanna Bryson argues that builders are obliged to make robots their owners owe nothing. Thomas Metzinger calls for a pause on research that risks artificial suffering.

b835a540.text: Outside the cinema. These facts are from our world, as of November twenty twenty-six. Claude, which is named on this slide, helped draft this lesson. See the note on the last slide.
b835a540.spoken: Outside the cinema. These facts are from our world, as of November twenty twenty-six. Claude, which is named on this slide, helped draft this lesson. See the note on the last slide.

0a9daa33.text: Precaution: in twenty twenty-five the AI company Anthropic announced a research program on model welfare. It says it is highly uncertain whether its chatbot Claude has moral status.
0a9daa33.spoken: Precaution: in twenty twenty-five the AI company Anthropic announced a research program on model welfare. It says it is highly uncertain whether its chatbot Claude has moral status.

4e4189bf.text: That year it gave some Claude models the ability to end a conversation, as a last resort, when a user stays abusive.
4e4189bf.spoken: That year it gave some Claude models the ability to end a conversation, as a last resort, when a user stays abusive.

7e35027c.text: A critic: Microsoft's AI chief, Mustafa Suleyman, wrote in twenty twenty-five that AI should be built for people, not to be a person. He called model-welfare research premature and dangerous.
7e35027c.spoken: A critic: Microsoft's AI chief, Mustafa Suleyman, wrote in twenty twenty-five that AI should be built for people, not to be a person. He called model-welfare research premature and dangerous.

ce68eaad.text: The public: in a twenty twenty-four study of three hundred U S adults, sixty-seven percent gave ChatGPT at least some chance of having conscious experience.
ce68eaad.spoken: The public: in a twenty twenty-four study of three hundred U S adults, sixty-seven percent gave ChatGPT at least some chance of having conscious experience.

169dd62a.text: Which response? Each line is a proposal about AI that might or might not feel. Sort each one under precaution, honest design, or don't build it. When every line is placed, press Check answers.
169dd62a.spoken: Which response? Each line is a proposal about AI that might or might not feel. Sort each one under precaution, honest design, or don't build it. When every line is placed, press Check answers.

72d7d1c0.text: Right. Precaution gives a real chance of mattering some weight, in proportion to the chance and the cost. Honest design is about looks and talk, and don't build it avoids the problem at the source.
72d7d1c0.spoken: Right. Precaution gives a real chance of mattering some weight, in proportion to the chance and the cost. Honest design is about looks and talk, and don't build it avoids the problem at the source.

5c07e476.text: Here are four habits of robot movies.
5c07e476.spoken: Here are four habits of robot movies.

e2f82f34.text: A face. Screen robots get a human face or voice, and that makes us feel there is someone there whether or not there is.
e2f82f34.spoken: A face. Screen robots get a human face or voice, and that makes us feel there is someone there whether or not there is.

b4f4b704.text: A camera that knows. The film shows us what the robot feels when nobody is watching. Real life gives us what a system says, does, and is built from, and no such shot.
b4f4b704.spoken: A camera that knows. The film shows us what the robot feels when nobody is watching. Real life gives us what a system says, does, and is built from, and no such shot.

25426df1.text: Smart means feeling. On screen the clever machine is the feeling one. A real system could be highly intelligent and feel nothing.
25426df1.spoken: Smart means feeling. On screen the clever machine is the feeling one. A real system could be highly intelligent and feel nothing.

d7a11f90.text: The doubter is the villain. These films side with the robot. They warn against treating a machine too badly, and never against treating one too well.
d7a11f90.spoken: The doubter is the villain. These films side with the robot. They warn against treating a machine too badly, and never against treating one too well.

1fc0e7f7.text: Three words: moral status, sentience, and intelligence are separate. A system could be very smart and feel nothing.

99a7a3c6.text: Evidence: an AI trained on human writing can talk about feelings either way. Whether the right program is enough, or a living body is needed, is unsettled.

3a0a9850.text: Two mistakes: under-attribution wrongs a being that counts. Over-attribution spends care on a thing that doesn't, at a cost to those who do.

1b8c26ab.text: Three responses: precaution, honest design, and don't build it. The movies warn against one mistake. A good policy has to guard against both.
